articles.title: La épica remontada de Lebrón y Augsburger que tumbó a Galán y Chingotto
articles.standfirst: El gaditano y el argentino empezaron perdiendo 6-0 y terminaron clasificándose a la final, donde se medirán contra Coello y Tapia
articles.summary: El gaditano y el argentino empezaron perdiendo 6-0 y terminaron clasificándose a la final, donde se medirán contra Coello y Tapia
articles.body: El espectáculo se adueñó del P1 de Milán con una remontada que entra dentro de la historia de Premier Padel. Chingalán salió a la pista decidido a dejar claro su hambre de título y dominó por completo el primer set, en el que pasó por encima de sus rivales con un contundente 6-0 y dos errores no forzados. En busca de una reacción en la segunda manga, Lebrón trataba de levantar el ánimo de su compañero, mientras la pareja número dos mantenía la calma durante el paso por los banquillos. Todo apuntaba a que Lebrón y Augsburger estaban fuera del partido y que la segunda semifinal tenía ya un desenlace claro. Sin embargo, los pupilos de Silingo comenzaron a encontrarse más cómodos sobre la pista, celebraron cada punto con mayor intensidad y recuperaron las buenas sensaciones en su juego. La reacción dio sus frutos y, con dos breaks de ventaja, sellaron el segundo set por un contundente 6-2. Con todo por decidir en el set definitivo, Lebrón y Augsburger mantuvieron la intensidad y volvieron a poner en aprietos a sus rivales al resto, alcanzando el 0-30 en sus dos primeros turnos de saque. Fue en el segundo cuando lograron abrir brecha en el marcador gracias a una bajada de revés de Lebrón desde el lado de su compañero. El break hizo mucho daño a Chingalán, que encajó una segunda rotura que terminó por sentenciar el encuentro. La distancia era ya demasiado grande y Galán, superado mentalmente por el desenlace, no encontró la manera de reaccionar ante el 6-2 definitivo. Juan y Leo desataron su alegría junto a su entrenador y compartieron la celebración con los miembros de su equipo presentes en la grada. Entre ellos se encontraba Juanma Rodríguez, entrenador de su academia, a quien Lebrón invitó a saltar a la pista para festejar con ellos una victoria cargada de emoción. Los Golden Boys quieren sellar cuanto antes una nueva temporada en lo más alto del pádel mundial y ni siquiera sus últimos rivales en las finales, Stupaczuk y Sanz, han encontrado la fórmula para frenarlos. Esta vez, el escenario fue la semifinal del Milano P1, donde ambos binomios volvieron a cruzarse con un desenlace idéntico al de sus enfrentamientos anteriores: nueva victoria para Coello y Tapia. Un triunfo con un significado especial para el vallisoletano, que alcanzó las 300 victorias en el circuito Premier Padel. El partido arrancó con mucha más igualdad que en sus dos duelos anteriores. Ambas parejas defendieron su servicio en los primeros compases, dando la sensación de que Jon Sanz y Franco Stupaczuk podían seguir el ritmo de los números uno. Sin embargo, con 4-3 en el marcador, Coello y Tapia dieron el primer golpe sobre la mesa con un quiebre que rompió el equilibrio. La reacción de sus rivales no tardó en llegar, aunque el intercambio de roturas terminó favoreciendo a los Golden Boys, que aprovecharon un remate fallido de Sanz para cerrar la primera manga por 6-4. El segundo golpe de Coello y Tapia sí hizo mella en la pareja dirigida por Pozzoni, que encajó un quiebre nada más arrancar la segunda manga. Con ventaja en el marcador, los Golden Boys se convierten en un rival todavía más temible. Los números uno elevaron el ritmo, desplegaron un auténtico vendaval de juego y generaron nuevas oportunidades de rotura en los siguientes turnos de saque de sus rivales, aunque sin llegar a materializarlas. Pese a ello, el quiebre inicial terminó siendo decisivo para decantar el encuentro. Coello y Tapia administraron su ventaja con autoridad y sellaron el triunfo por 6-3, certificando su pase a la final del Milano P1.

articles.title: Clayton Young defies doctor’s four-week rest advice to run Chicago Marathon personal best with hamstring tear
articles.summary: American runner Clayton Young finished the 2026 Chicago Marathon in 2:05:23 despite a 12-centimeter tear in his hamstring tendon.
articles.body: American runner Clayton Young finished the 2026 Chicago Marathon in 2:05:23 despite a 12-centimeter tear in his hamstring tendon. The October 11 race gave him a personal best and made him the top American man, but reaching the starting line was far from certain. His first doctor had advised him to rest for four weeks. Now, Young has shared how his faith and his wife, Ashley, helped him through those difficult weeks. He also has his sights set on the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Clayton Young Reveals How a Hamstring Tear Put His Chicago Marathon Plans at RiskIn an October 15 conversation with CITIUS MAG host Chris Chavez, Young explained that he wanted to give himself every chance to race. He had also hoped to challenge the American marathon record of 2:04:43, set by his training partner Conner Mantz in 2025.When Chavez asked if he believed the record was possible, Young replied, “Yeah. Yeah, I mean, or at least I believe that I would do everything I could until I was told not to.”The injury became a concern after the Great North Run in England on September 13. With around 250 metres left in the half-marathon, Young felt his hamstring tighten and had to slow down. He finished seventh in 1:02:04, but the pain did not go away.After cutting a speed workout short, Young underwent an MRI on September 17. The scan showed a 12-centimeter tear in an upper hamstring tendon near the pelvis. His first doctor recommended a platelet-rich plasma injection and four weeks without running. Following that advice would have ended his hopes of competing in Chicago.Young then sought further medical advice and worked with his coach, Ed Eyestone, to adjust his training. He completed a 22-mile run and returned to faster sessions while keeping a close eye on the injury. His hamstring was still not fully healed when he reached the starting line.The physical challenge was only part of the story. Young said the experience also changed how he viewed his faith. He and Ashley leaned on prayer and support from people around them while trying to decide what to do next.“These last four weeks from a faith standpoint have never… I want to be respectful of everybody in their faith. But I’m going to look back on these last four weeks with more faith building experience than I’ve ever seen,” Young said.He added that the couple kept finding reasons to move forward even when running seemed like the wrong choice.“When everything said, don’t run this race, it was so interesting to see how so many of the answers that we were receiving were just like, keep moving forward, take the next step, and trust in God and the plan that he has for you, even though it doesn’t make sense,” he said.Ashley remained by his side throughout the difficult period. Young said the experience brought them closer and strengthened their faith. “Yeah, Ashley and I grew stronger together. Our faith grew stronger together. And yeah, I’m going to look back at this as a miracle,” he said.Young later confirmed that his hamstring had not fully recovered. “My hamstring held up. No, it wasn’t made perfect, but we got through this,” he said.Clayton Young Targets LA 2028 Olympics After Chicago Marathon Personal BestYoung finished seventh overall in Chicago with a time of 2:05:23. According to USA Track & Field, the result made him the second-fastest American man ever on a course eligible for records. It also improved his previous best on such a course, which was 2:08:00 at the 2023 Chicago Marathon.His next major goal is the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. In an interview with Men’s Health earlier this year, Young said, “My biggest goals right now are to do everything I can to prepare for the LA 2028 Olympic Games.”Young already has Olympic experience. He finished second at the 2024 U.S. Olympic Marathon Trials before placing ninth in the marathon at the Paris Games. He now has another personal best to build on as he works toward a return to the Olympic stage.For now, his hamstring recovery will be important as he plans his next races. articles.title: Ohio State shatters Indiana’s 22-game winning streak, but questions linger about Julian Sayin's health
articles.summary: Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith scored the game-winning touchdown after admitting he ran the wrong route, ending Indiana's 22-game winning streak.
articles.body: BLOOMINGTON, IN - The biggest home game in Indiana history was ruined by Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith, and a Hoosiers foot that was just out of bounds. For the past 14 months, the talk of college football has centered around the Hoosiers stacking up wins and a national championship. All the while, the Buckeyes just sat quietly in the background with the best player in the sport, waiting for their turn to prove the doubters wrong after a loss at Texas earlier in the season thanks to a fourth quarter collapse. Even though Julian Sayin did not have his most productive outing on Saturday, all he needed was his Heisman Trophy candidate Jeremiah Smith to bail him out a time or two en route to a close-shave 19-15 victory over the Hoosiers. Plenty of times this afternoon in Bloomington, it felt as though this Ohio State team was just one play away from ending the party. But, with Josh Hoover throwing a touchdown pass with just over 10:12 remaining in the fourth quarter, we found ourselves wondering if the Buckeyes would once again blow a fourth quarter lead. COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S CHAOS ERA IS HERE: TEXAS RALLIES, OREGON FALLS AND LANE KIFFIN EYES RETURN TO OLE MISS As 1:02 was remaining in the game, the Indiana crowd bursted into cheers after Nick Marsh came down with what the Hoosiers thought would be the go-ahead touchdown catch in what would be one of the wilder endings we've seen this season. Turns out, it was one of the crazier plays we've witnessed, but for all the wrong reasons for Indiana, as Nick Marsh immediately signaled by grabbing his helmet. As the fireworks went off inside Memorial Stadium, the mood quickly shifted within the hearts of Hoosier fans, as Nick Marsh was ruled to be out of bounds when he caught the football, sending the Ohio State sideline into a frenzy of joy. "We had it, but we just didn’t make it happen," Curt Cignetti said following the loss. "It's a hard one to swallow, learn from it and move on." Hoosiers have to start fresh, while Buckeyes are looking for a short-term QB A 22-game winning streak for Indiana came to an end, while Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia jubilantly told assistant coaches after the game that he'd rather not watch the final play over again. What we witnessed on this chilly day in Bloomington will go down as one of the most complicated games over the past few seasons for both teams. INDIANA'S BATTLE AGAINST OHIO STATE AT MEMORIAL STADIUM HIGHLIGHTS HOOSIERS' STRONG COMMITMENT TO THE MILITARY Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin will at the very least be out a "couple of weeks", according to head coach Ryan Day following the game, after suffering a shoulder injury during the fourth quarter that saw him return to the sidelines wearing a sling. Ohio State does have a bye next week, before a trip to USC in late October. Everything was starting to come up roses for the defending national champions during a frantic fourth quarter, which also saw Jeremiah Smith give the Buckeyes the eventual game-winning touchdown. "I actually ran the wrong route," Smith said postgame. But, Julian (Sayin) trusted me and I made the play." This Big Ten game lived up to the hype, at least with theatrics The pageantry of college football was on display for the few days leading up to this top-five showdown in Bloomington, as fans flocked to town in hopes of seeing Indiana extend its winning streak to 23 games. But, the heartbreak would come sneaking around the bend over what might be the wildest 20 seconds of recent Big Ten memory, thanks to the insane final few minutes. NICK SABAN AND TIM TEBOW GIVE THEIR THOUGHTS ON EXPANDING THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF TO 24 TEAMS Is this the defining game for an Ohio State football team that has all the potential to be inside Lucas Oil Stadium at regular season's end for a Big Ten title game? Absolutely, but they'll have to get through the next month without a starting quarterback who nearly cost them the game on multiple occasions on Saturday. In what was actually an uneventful game for nearly three full quarters, each squad decided to save their best theatrics until the final minutes. It's no secret that this unit is not fundamentally the same as we witnessed last season, but that doesn’t mean Curt Cignetti's squad can't put itself in a position to hoist the Big Ten trophy once again. But, the Hoosiers will need more out of their starting quarterback, along with a group of wide receivers who found themselves looking over their heads numerous times against the Buckeyes. Who knows, maybe they put it all together, but judging by what we witnessed on Saturday, there are plenty of things to fix if they are going to make another CFP run. articles.title: GAME THREAD: Cougs look to get right at Oregon State
articles.summary: Good afternoon, Cougar football fans. Tonight, your 1-5 Washington State Cougars travel down to Corvallis to square off with the 4-2 Oregon State Beavers. Bo...
articles.body:
Tonight, your 1-5 Washington State Cougars travel down to Corvallis to square off with the 4-2 Oregon State Beavers.

Both teams are rolling in off complete opposite ends of the momentum scale. For WSU, they are losers of three straight and have netted just three offensive touchdowns in those losses. Their lone win came nearly a month ago against FCS Duquesne. The Cougars are also 0-2 to start Pac-12 play with losses to Fresno State and most recently last week at Utah State.

With the offense coming in as one of the worst in football, head coach Kirby Moore has elected to make a change at quarterback. Redshirt freshman Owen Eshelman will be the starter for the Cougars tonight, making his first career start and his second appearance. He briefly appeared late in the win over Duquesne but didn't appear in the stat sheet, as he handed the ball to Leo Pulalasi twice before the game ended. Eshelman will look to spark an offense that put up a bleak 64 yards of total offense in the second half against Utah State.

As for the Beavers, it's been a rosy start for new head coach Jamarcus Shepherd. After dropping their first two games in close fashion to ranked teams in Houston and Texas Tech, the Beavers have won four in a row—including two against Pac-12 foes—and have averaged 51.8 points in those games. Last week, the Beavers trounced San Diego State, 66-14. At halftime in that game, the Beavers were already ahead 38-7. Quarterback Brady Atkinson finished the game with 409 passing yards and five touchdowns. But the real story of the Beaver offense is phenom wide receiver Jesse Legree, who had 10 catches for 191 yards and a trio of touchdowns. Legree nearly had as many receiving yards as WSU had total offense last week. So far this season, Legree has 38 receptions for a nation leading 932 yards and 12 touchdowns.

The Cougars and Beavers will also apparently be playing for a trophy for what is believed to be the first time in this long rivalry.

It was understandable given Baltimore's star power and status in the league. While the Falcons were unfortunate to fall short, the game still gave viewers a clear look at where Kevin Stefanski's team failed to produce.

They were all over the place trying to contain a heavy zone-based running game. The Ravens will run over plenty of teams with Derrick Henry leading the charge. It remains alarming how incapable the Falcons were at times of getting off blocks. The inability to convert pressure into sacks was frustrating against a backup quarterback. Missing several open-field tackles led to allowing more explosive plays.

For all their defensive struggles, fans believe the issues in the dropback passing game need to be addressed the most. Michael Penix Jr. looked rattled by Jesse Minter's varied looks and didn't come close to converting in pure dropback situations on third-and-long.

Although he started to connect with Drake London in the second half, the offense is too talented and well-coached to be completely overwhelmed. That forced the defense on the field for long stretches, leading to them collapsing late in the game.

Penix Jr. has played well in his return, but his tendency to panic in the pocket under duress and struggle to create out of structure leaves the passing game somewhat limited. That is where he'll need to improve, as well as the coaching staff's ability to get more on early downs when they can't impose their will on the ground.

The disappointing loss hasn't damaged the fanbase's belief in the team's direction, as they remain confident going forward.

articles.title: Why military day meant so much to Clemson OL who led Tigers down The Hill with American flag
articles.summary: Elyjah Thurmon got to honor his military family on Military Appreciation Day, while Vic Burley and Chris Johnson Jr. earned breakthrough moments.
articles.body:
CLEMSON — Clemson football's game vs. Charleston Southern was a special day for offensive lineman Elyjah Thurmon.

The Tigers (4-2) defeated the Buccaneers (3-4) on their annual Military Appreciation Day 37-0. Thurmon, who comes from a military family, got to carry an American flag and lead Clemson down The Hill at Memorial Stadium to mark the occasion.

Thurmon's parents, Tammie Williams and Earnest Thurmon, are U.S. Army veterans. Thurmon's grandfather, Walter Williams, and great-uncle, David Harris, served in the Army and the Marines, respectively. Thurmon's parents were honored on the field during the first quarter, and Thurmon got to stand alongside them.

Thurmon said he was full of excitement throughout game day.

"I can't explain how happy I was," Thurmon said. "Once I got off the bus and stood in front of the entire crowd on The Hill with the flag in my hand, I kinda blacked out for a second. I was so happy."

Clemson football vs Charleston Southern: Dabo Swinney, Tait Reynolds see our top photos

Thurmon said being in a military family, and the strict structure that comes with it, has shaped his entire life. Thurmon is even thinking about joining the Army if his days playing football end soon.

"Once my career ends, if anything else doesn't work out, go serve," said Thurmon, who is a junior. "It wouldn't hurt."

Vic Burley earns first big moment since suspension

Oct. 17 was also a big day for defensive tackle Vic Burley, who earned his first full sack as a Tiger in the fourth quarter against Charleston Southern.

Burley was suspended for the first two games of the season by Clemson coach Dabo Swinney after being arrested and charged with public disorderly conduct on Aug. 22. Swinney reinstated Burley ahead of the North Carolina game on Sept. 19, but he's played sparingly, as Swinney thinks Burley fell behind on conditioning.

The Charleston Southern game was the most Burley has played since coming back. He said he's glad that Swinney and his teammates have accepted him back.

"I learned not to take things for granted," Burley said of what he learned during his suspension. "I mean, I didn't really take it for granted, but just watching the game that I love being stripped away from me, and not being able to do it, just gives you a new appreciation for the game."

Chris Johnson Jr. scores first Clemson touchdowns

There was much interest in running back Chris Johnson Jr. when he transferred from SMU. However, he only rushed for 107 yards in Clemson's first five games.

Johnson had 34 rushing yards against the Buccaneers, but he did score his first two Clemson touchdowns. One was a 6-yard rush in the first quarter for the Tigers' first touchdown, and another was a 2-yard rush in the second quarter.

"I think that's a good start," Johnson said. "We still got a long stretch to go, so that was a good thing."

articles.title: The Top 2026 Cubs Batters Entering Free Agency
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs had a dangerous offense in 2026, but the Cubs' free agent batters could change that. Chicago's pitching staff has multiple free agents and i...
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs had a dangerous offense in 2026, but the Cubs' free agent batters could change that. Chicago's pitching staff has multiple free agents and is controlling the narrative. However, their outfield is set to lose nearly as much as the rotation. If Chicago wants to bounce back in 2027, it needs to improve the roster, and that starts with the Cubs' free agent batters.

Without a doubt, Seiya Suzuki is the biggest Cubs free agent batter. The right fielder is not only the team's top free agent , but one of the best hitters available. This season, he hit .270 with 26 home runs and 86 RBI. Suzuki vastly improved his defense and is a Gold Glove finalist.

Over the past five seasons with the Cubs, Suzuki hit .269 with 113 home runs. He has been one of their best power bats and a valuable piece of the lineup. One of the Cubs' biggest needs , as four players are leaving. Losing Suzuki would leave a major gap in the team's lineup. Unfortunately, if the Cubs wish to keep him, they will need to enter a bidding war. Several teams will show interest, and he will be expensive. Chicago has the money to keep him, but it is hard to say if they want to give another hitter a large contract. He should be their top offensive priority, but his future with the Cubs is very hard to predict.

Speaking of the outfield situation, Ian Happ will be a free agent. This means the Cubs may lose their two starting corner outfielders. Happ should be cheaper, but his struggles this past season make it hard to pay much for him.

Happ is still an elite defender who can provide 20 home runs a season. However, his batting average is no longer as solid as it used to be. Many believe he may have played his last game with the Cubs . Unless he takes a large hometown discount, I have trouble seeing the Cubs pay enough to keep him. He has had a great career in Chicago, and of all the Cubs free agents, he may be the hardest to say goodbye to.

Michael Conforto was brought in as a solid depth piece and was exactly that. The veteran had a .240 batting average, 15 home runs, and 45 RBI. Although he had some quality starts, his best moments came as a pinch hitter. When the team needed a crazy comeback, Conforto seemed to be involved.

It will be interesting to see what Conforto can get in the open market. I don't see him being too expensive, but a team could give him a solid payday, hoping he reverts to the player he used to be. If he is willing to platoon, it would be great to see him back as a depth outfielder. It just feels like he could get a bigger role/more money elsewhere.

Of the Cubs free agent batters, Tyrone Taylor is one of the harder ones to predict. Chicago acquired him in the Clay Holmes trade, and he exceeded expectations. In Chicago, he hit .351 and destroyed left-handed pitchers. His versatility at all three outfield positions made him a great depth piece. He was here less than the other three, but still gave the Cubs solid moments.

The same issue with Conforto arises here. Other teams may offer to give him a starting role and/or more money. He looked great when in Chicago, but I don't know if the Cubs saw enough to give him a large payday. Taylor could be a great depth piece, but once again, he seems destined for a larger role. Bringing back at least one of Taylor/Conforto could be a huge piece in stabilizing the Cubs outfield.

Tyler Austin is the least known of the Cubs free agent batters. He signed last offseason as Michael Busch 's backup. Austin then missed the entire season with a knee injury. He was rarely discussed, and it's impossible to say how the coaching staff feels about him. If it was a minimum-level deal, Chicago could explore bringing him back. However, the Cubs will likely look elsewhere for more proven talent.

The Last Word on the Cubs Free Agent Batters

The list of Cubs free agent batters isn't as lengthy as the pitching free agents, but it's a critical storyline. The outfield could look entirely different. Ideally, they could bring back one of the starters and one backup, but that depends on how free agency plays out. Besides catcher, the team's other starting positions are full. Chicago has the talent, so filling the outfield is crucial to return to the playoffs.

articles.title: How Tramell Jones Jr. stayed ready for his moment in Florida football’s upset of Texas
articles.summary: Tramell Jones Jr. threw two touchdowns in his first career start, leading Florida football to an upset of No. 6 Texas.
articles.body:
AUSTIN, Texas – The circumstances didn't matter to Florida football's Tramell Jones Jr.

It didn't matter that he didn't win the starting quarterback job in the offseason. Nor did he care that he had the tough task of making his first career start against No. 6 Texas.

All that mattered was staying ready, just as he had been all season.

"I was preparing like I was a starter every week, so this week was no different for me," Jones said. "But just preparing, taking reps 100%.

That preparation paid off Saturday, as Jones helped lead Florida to an improbable 27-24 upset against the Longhorns. It's why Florida coach Jon Sumrall reiterated earlier in the week that he believed the Gators can win with Jones at quarterback.

"For his first opportunity, even when he didn't make some throws he needed to make, he kept battling and kept fighting, and that's when good things happen," Sumrall said. "And so I'm proud of him for staying resilient, through going back to training camp when he didn't win the job, and still being ready."

Jones learned Friday that he was named starter as Aaron Philo continued to deal with a shoulder injury.

"We knew it all week, pretty much," Sumrall said. "All you had to be able to do to figure that out was have a pulse. But what I would say is, through maybe some things that didn't go well for him in the game, he stayed steady and responded, and he'd miss a throw and come back and make a throw."

Jones wasn't rattled by an ugly start as Florida (5-2, 3-2 SEC) went 0-for-7 on third-down conversions in the first half, trailing 17-3 to Texas (4-2, 1-2).

But things turned around for Jones just after missing a wide-open Eric Singleton for what could have been a touchdown. Instead of getting rattled, he settled in.

"I overthrew Eric in practice, so I was kind of aiming it," Jones said. "I can hit those kind of footballs. I just got to lay it out there. Eric's a fast guy; he can go get it. So I got to trust him.

Jones responded on fourth-and-12, threading a pass to Dallas Wilson along the sideline for a 17-yard gain. The conversion helped set up Florida's first touchdown and kick-started a stretch in which the Gators scored 24 unanswered points.

"Just taking play-by-play, hitting Dallas, trusting him to go flat on flood route, and we converted," Jones said. "It gave the team a spark, and that's what we needed. Started off slow, didn't play nowhere near perfect. But the team was behind me."

Check out our Florida football vs Texas photo gallery: Best images

In similar fashion, out of the half, Jones orchestrated another scoring drive to tie the game as Jones went 5-for-5 on third-down plays.

"I think he played great. I've been saying this for a long time," said Florida running back Jadan Baugh, who delivered a late touchdown to seal the win. "As soon as he got here as a freshman. I said Tramell's going to be a great quarterback because he has that grit, he has that want-to."

Jones finished 22-for-35 for 155 yards and two touchdowns while scrambling for 41 yards to complete the upset.

"It's pretty big," Jones said. "But I've been playing football all my life. I just took it in as another football game, coming in here and playing the game I've been playing all my life."

Now as the Gators head to the open week, it'll be seen if Florida makes a change under center in preparation for No. 1 Georgia.

"I know that's going to be everybody's question probably," Sumrall said. "I would say this: I'm going to get, I'm going to watch the tape; the whole staff will. I'm happy for Tramell and his success. He missed plenty of things today. He did some good things today. The success with our team today had more to do than just the quarterback.

"There's going to be no decision tonight of like, here's what I'm doing moving forward. Philo's been our guy and has won us some big games, too. Just like Tramell helped us win a big game today as well. So I like both guys. I love both guys. I believe in both guys."

articles.title: Hoover's Alex Hobe earns first win at Federal League cross country meet
articles.summary: A first-time winner, a back-to-back champion and a team title sweep in a coach's final season highlighted the Federal League cross country meet.
articles.body:
PLAIN TWP. — Green's Lucy Sveda went to the Federal League Cross Country Championships hoping to repeat.

Hoover's Alex Hobe went there hoping to win, period.

The wait is worth it if your first high school win comes at your last conference meet. Hobe broke the ice on Oct. 17 when he captured the Federal League boys title in 15:53.3.

Our best photos from 2026 Stark County Cross Country Championships

"Getting a win is really special, and this is probably one of the best moments I've ever had," Hobe said. "My freshman year, I had a stress fracture. I couldn't run all year. I just remember watching from the sidelines, always wanting to run this race.

"I never thought I would be able to win, so glory to God. That was a special feeling knowing all the work I did finally paid off."

Sveda defended her title in the girls race. The Jackson Polar Bears sent retiring head coach Kevin Walsh out with two more Federal League championships as they swept the boys and girls team titles.

Alex Hobe pushed by Hoover teammate before pulling away

Hobe and Hoover teammate Sam Baker ran neck-and-neck ahead of the pack during the first half of the race. With Baker having a couple of wins under his belt this season, Hobe knew he would be pressed.

"Sam has been great the whole year," Hobe said. "He came out of nowhere last year at this meet."

Hobe made his move after he and Baker hit the final third of the race. He finished 10 seconds ahead of Baker.

"When I got to the two-mile mark, Sam was still really close to me and I started to gap it," Hobe said. "I knew we had 1-2 but I really wanted to get that win. I just trusted my strength and started to push it."

Green's Lucy Sveda maintains lead in defending girls title

Sveda won the girls race by just over 43 seconds. Her time of 18:47.4 matched last year's winning mark when she edged the field by just under two seconds.

"Having that title last year just gave me the motivation to keep it going," Sveda said. "I really wanted to make my senior year something special. Defending the title was something I really wanted to do.

"I just tried to maintain my pace throughout. The goal was to go sub-18. I didn't get that, but I did maintain the lead with a pretty good gap. Knowing that I could hold that lead is what kept me going."

Sveda hopes she can make a big impact in her final high school postseason. She qualified for the state meet for the first time as a junior.

"I just want to make it to regionals and state and we'll just see how it goes from there," Sveda said.

Jackson coach Kevin Walsh celebrates two more titles in final Federal League meet

Jackson's team title sweep came in Walsh's final meet as head coach on his home course. He will retire after this season after coaching the Polar Bears boys to Division I state championship in 2023 and the girls to a Division I state runner-up finish in 2005. Both teams have also won several Federal League titles under him.

"I just couldn't be any prouder of the kids," Walsh said. "I'm blessed to be part of this league. It has been a great joy. To leave on top in a league that is so amazing with so many great friends is very special."

Hoover pushed Jackson to the brink in the boys race. The Polar Bears edged the Vikings by just two points to win their sixth straight league title. Liam Barry came in fourth to lead Jackson. Baron Memmer and Colin Crawford also finished in the top 10.

"I thought that last 800 really made a big difference," Walsh said. "You could tell they wanted it. I knew it meant something to them to send me out on a good way."

The Polar Bears won the girls meet by 31 points. Bryn Ball finished second and Abby Parsons came in third to lead Jackson. Liv Ziders also finished sixth.

COOKEVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Jax Leatherwood threw three touchdowns passes to lead Tennessee Tech to a 49-20 victory over Eastern Kentucky on Saturday.

Leatherwood was 22-of-30 passing for 199 yards. M.J. Flowers ran for 108 yards and a touchdown and Qua Ashley added 77 yards rushing and two scores for Tennessee Tech (6-1), ranked No. 15 in the Stats Perform poll.

Leatherwood threw a 36-yard touchdown pass to Tre' Holloway to cap Tennessee Tech's first drive of the game. Ashley scored on a 2-yard run, Jameson Wharton had a 21-yard pick-6, Leatherwood added a 19-yard touchdown pass to Eric Weatherly, and the Golden Eagles took a 28-7 lead into the break.

Ashley's 42-yard touchdown run made it 42-7 midway through the third quarter.

Ryder Hooks had a 44-yard touchdown run and finished with 166 yards on the ground for Eastern Kentucky (2-5). Jeffrey Kinley returned an interception 95 yards for a score for the Colonels in the first quarter.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley 2: LIVE round-by-round updates
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois, Fabio Wardley clash again in London on Saturday
articles.body:
MMA Fighting has Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley 2 live round-by-round updates for one of the most anticipated boxing fights of the year at O2 Arena in London, England, on Saturday afternoon.

The main event is expected to begin around 5:30 p.m. on DAZN. Check out our Dubois vs. Wardley 2 results page to find out what happened on the undercard.

Daniel Dubois (23-3, 22 knockouts) won the WBO heavyweight title in their first meeting this year with a 11th-round knockout of Wardley this past May.

Fabio Wardley (20-1-1, 19 knockouts) suffered his first career loss against Dubois. He had won three straight heading into their first fight together.

Check out the Dubois vs. Wardley 2 round-by-round live blog below.

Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley 2 Live Blog

The rematch of one of the best fights of the year is just around the corner.

Fabio Wardley and Daniel Dubois make the walk now.

Referee Steve Gray oversees this championship bout.

The crowd is buzzing. Somebody gonna get hurt.

Dubois strikes first with a jab, and seconds later connects with a right that wobbles Wardley! Wow! He touches canvas and we have our first 10-count, Wardley answers. Dubois right back on the offensive, not sure Wardley has recovered at all. Dubois sizing him up, he doubles up on the jab and fires in another right. Wardley still finding his legs here. Two more big punches from Dubois, he's landing big, but making sure not to punch himself out.

Wardley throws a right back, but he's short, and Dubois advances again. He's letting the right hand go and it feels like he's just inches away from connecting with the fight-ender. Wardley jabs the body. Dubois with another rocking right, Wardley on the ropes, just eating punches. Gray lets this fight go with 10 seconds remaining in the round and Wardley makes it out of the round despite heavy pressure from Dubois. Intense first three minutes.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-7, Dubois.

Wardley comes out swinging, to his credit. Offense might be the best defense at this point, because Dubois was surgical in Round 1. Dubois jabs his way in, Wardley with a quick tie-up. Both fighters a little cautious here, Dubois not wanting to get caught by a counter, Wardley aware of Dubois' power. Dubois with another sharp 1-2 and Wardley takes the right on the chin. Not sure how much more of those he can take. Big miss by Wardley, and Dubois capitalizes with a flurry of punches. He's just blasting Wardley, and Wardley's corner has seen enough. The towel is thrown in. Dubois does it again.

Official result: Daniel Dubois def. Fabio Wardley via second-round TKO (corner retirement) (2:21)

Dubois calls Wardley a great warrior, but that "it is my time and my era."

"I had bad intentions from the beginning and this is God's victory tonight, we done well."

He says his back was against the wall in the first fight and tonight was about "showing that we mean business."

It's time to talk about Dubois' next opponent, and promoter Frank Warren says there are a number of unification bouts for the WBO heavyweight champion, but they don't call out any specific names. Dubois just says he wants "big money and big fights."

IBF champion Filip Hrgovic is in the crowd and Warren calls him into the ring for an impromptu face off with Dubois.

Hrgovic says Dubois had an "easy night" and suggests he be ready to fight in March. Dubois sounds interested in running it back after he handed Hrgovic his first pro loss when they fought for an interim IBF belt in 2024.

articles.title: New NHL Rumors Update Connor Hellebuyck's Jets Suspension Timeline After Goalie's Trade Request
articles.summary: The Winnipeg Jets reportedly have a deadline coming up in their ongoing stalemate with discontented star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck.
articles.body:
The Winnipeg Jets reportedly have a deadline coming up in their ongoing stalemate with discontented star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck.

The suspension issued to Hellebuyck for failing to report to training camp is expected to expire next Friday, The Athletic's Chris Johnston and Murat Ates reported Saturday.

Johnston and Ates noted Hellebuyck's "immediate future remains up in the air" because the Jets "have not been offered a trade they deem fair."

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Hellebuyck did not participate in training camp in September but told the Jets before their Oct. 2 season opener he intended to report to the team.

The Jets kept Hellebuyck suspended after that point under a clause in the CBA that allows teams to issue "a disciplinary suspension of reasonable length" to players who miss training camp, according to Friedman.

The suspension will have cost Hellebuyck more than $925,000 in forfeited salary by next Friday, per Johnston and Ates.

Hellebuyck, a three-time Vezina Trophy winner, marked a career-low .895 save percentage last season as the Jets went 35-35-12 and missed the playoffs.

He first announced in late August he had requested a trade from the Jets "several months ago."

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported in mid-September that Hellebuyck had informed the Jets he would not be reporting to camp.

Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff said the following day he wanted to prioritize getting the Hellebuyck trade "right" rather than making a quick deal.

The Edmonton Oilers make sense as a trade suitor for Hellebuyck, although TSN's Pierre LeBrun has said Hellebuyck has no interest in playing for a Canadian team.

Hellebuyck was linked earlier this offseason to the Buffalo Sabres, but Sportsnet's Nick Kypreos reported the Sabres were unwilling to include Zach Benson in a potential deal.

Other teams tied to an interest in Hellebuyck include the Carolina Hurricanes and Los Angeles Kings, per Friedman and Sportsnet's Frank Seravalli .

Hellebuyck has a full no-move clause this season, per PuckPedia , so both he and the Jets would get to weigh in on any potential move.

Whether Hellebuyck is traded by next Friday will determine whether he ultimately considers playing another game in Winnipeg, where the Jets are off to a 4-1-2 start to the 2026-27 season with Stuart Skinner as their primary starter.

articles.title: Golden State Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes exits WNBA Finals after falling on face
articles.summary: Golden State Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes was injured against the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday, Oct. 17.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO ― Golden State Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes took a hard fall and exited Game 1 of the WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream with an apparent injury.

Hayes nearly came up with a steal in the fourth quarter with about 2 minutes, 38 seconds left in the game when she dove for a loose ball, narrowly missing, instead faceplanting on the hardwood.

Hayes stayed down on the ground for a few minutes before the Valkyries medical staff and coaches came to the middle of the floor to tend to their veteran guard.

She was eventually helped up and she walked to the locker room on her own merit with medical staff and trainers following closely behind.

Hayes scored 3 points in 24 minutes of playing time shooting 1-for-12. She added six rebounds and four assists before leaving the game.

The Valkyries did not immediately have an update on Hayes following her exit.

articles.summary: PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve Saturday, two days after the Philadelphia Eagles revealed he has a blood clot in hi...
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve Saturday, two days after the Philadelphia Eagles revealed he has a blood clot in his calf .

Hurts was initially ruled out Thursday for the Eagles' upcoming game against Carolina. The Eagles said then that Hurts was injured when he took a cleat to his calf area on Oct. 4 against the Los Angeles Rams.

Hurts informed the medical staff of the injury after practice on Oct. 8. The Super Bowl 59 MVP was back at practice the next day before the team left for London to play Jacksonville.

"Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday (Oct. 10) following the team's flight to London and walk-through," the Eagles said in Thursday's statement. "The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia."

articles.title: Cornell defeats Lehigh 48-38 for first win over top-5 team since 1939
articles.summary: (AP) — Garrett Bass-Sulpizio threw for a career-high 366 yards to go with his career-high 103 yards rushing and Cornell defeated Lehigh 48-38 on Saturday for...
articles.body:
ITHACA, N.Y. (AP) — Garrett Bass-Sulpizio threw for a career-high 366 yards to go with his career-high 103 yards rushing and Cornell defeated Lehigh 48-38 on Saturday for the Big Red's first win over a top-five team since 1939.

Lehigh, which entered as the No. 4 team in the Stats Perform FCS Top 25, fell behind 14-0 in the first quarter and was never able to catch up.

Cornell, which was 2-10-2 all-time against top-10 opponents, last defeated a top-10 team when the Big Red beat No. 4 Ohio State in 1939. No. 5 Dartmouth fell in 1938.

Cornell (3-2) rolled up 410 yards and 31 points in the first half. Bass-Sulpizio had five completions of 20 or more yards, including a 37-yard touchdown pass to Ja'von Broussard, and Cornell led 31-17 at halftime.

Lehigh scored three touchdowns in the second half, two on passes by Derek Morgan, and the third on a short run by Luke Yoder. The Mountain Hawks drew within seven points with each score, but each time the Big Red had an answer.

Yoder's 3-yard run made it 38-31 early in the fourth quarter, then Cornell drove 81 yards to Jordan Triplett's 3-yard touchdown run and a 45-31 lead.

Lehigh made it 45-38 on Morgan's 41-yard strike to Bryce Werner, then Cornell added a field goal.

Morgan was intercepted on Lehigh's final drive.

Lehigh was outgained 311 to minus-3 in the first quarter. The Mountain Hawks went three-and-out on their only two possessions of the quarter but got on the board when Luke Denny recovered a Cornell fumble in the end zone and returned it 100-plus yards for a touchdown.

Morgan had three touchdowns and 204 yards passing and Yoder ran for 142 yards for Lehigh (6-1).

The NBA champion guard previously helped the Denver Nuggets capture their first championship in 2023 , establishing himself as a versatile contributor capable of providing defense, playmaking and experience off the bench.

However, New York's limited financial flexibility complicated its roster decisions heading into the regular season.

Brown recently discussed the c hallenges facing veteran players under the NBA's collective bargaining agreement , particularly those seeking contracts below the league's maximum salary tier.

"I'm sure there is (frustration). The new CBA is good for max guys, new free agents and rookie extension guys. The middle guys, it kind of sucks for us. There's not a lot of people getting that full mid-level," Brown said, via SNY Knicks on X. "But that's just the way it is right now."

Meanwhile, Wiseman's inclusion provides New York with additional frontcourt depth as the franchise prepares to defend its championship.

articles.title: Freshman's 4 goals lead Wisconsin women's hockey rout of Minnesota State
articles.summary: Rosalie Tremblay scored four goals and Cassie Hall extended her season-opening goal-scoring streak to eight games for the second-ranked Badgers.
articles.body:
Canadian freshman forward Rosalie Tremblay made up for lost time with the Wisconsin women's hockey team , scoring four goals Oct. 17 in a 12-1 victory over Minnesota State at LaBahn Arena in Madison.

The second-ranked Badgers (6-2-0, 2-2-0 WCHA) were coming off a pair of losses to now-No. 1 Ohio State. Tremblay and defenders Ava Murphy and Emma Venusio missed that road series while at training camp with the Canadian national team .

Tremblay scored UW's first goal 12 minutes 4 seconds into the afternoon game, added one in the second period and then picked up her third and fourth goals in a span of two minutes late in the third.

Senior forward Cassie Hall extended her goal scoring streak to eight games when she gave UW a 6-0 lead midway through the second period.

The Badgers put 62 shots on goal to 23 for the Mavericks (2-4-0, 0-4-0) and scored six goals in the final period.

In the series opener the night before, in which UW scored four goals in the third of a 5-1 victory , Slovakian freshman Nela Lopušanová managed four points on a goal and three assists.

articles.title: Why Michigan benched Bryce Underwood vs. Penn State
articles.summary: This is a big move for the Wolverines.
articles.body:
Michigan made the tough decision to bench quarterback Bryce Underwood at halftime of the team's home game against Penn State on Saturday.

What prompted the decision? Well, Underwood went 5-for-11 for 43 yards and two interceptions in the first half of Saturday's game.

That combines with previous season struggles that left Wolverines fans wondering just how much room Underwood had before the team benched him for freshman Tommy Carr.

We're not sure what this means for Underwood going forward, but Carr could play himself into a starting job if he's successful on the field. Underwood would be a highly sought-after transfer if he left Michigan.

We'll see what's next for Underwood and Michigan after the game.

The team hosts Indiana next Saturday at noon ET.

articles.title: Jerry Jeudy leads Browns' threats the Ravens cannot afford to overlook
articles.summary: The Ravens must account for Cleveland's supporting cast, from Jerry Jeudy's big-play ability to defensive playmakers and Raheim Sanders.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens know that divisional games rarely unfold exactly as expected. A team can spend the week preparing for its opponent's biggest names only to find that a lesser-discussed player makes the decisive contribution. That is the challenge facing Baltimore as it prepares to face the Cleveland Browns , whose supporting cast includes several players capable of complicating the matchup.

From a receiver who can change a game with one opportunity to defensive contributors who can disrupt the Ravens ' offense, Cleveland has options Baltimore cannot afford to overlook. The Browns also have a potential backfield change if Quinshon Judkins is limited, so Baltimore should prepare for more than one version of Cleveland's game plan.

Jerry Jeudy has already shown what he can accomplish in Cleveland. After falling out of favor with the Denver Broncos , he joined the Browns and earned a Pro Bowl selection in his first season. He hasn't been the focal point of Cleveland's offense this season, but his ability to create separation and make a game-changing play makes him dangerous whenever the ball comes his way.

The Ravens must avoid treating Jeudy as a secondary concern just because he hasn't commanded the offense's full attention. Baltimore's defensive backs will need to communicate through coverage adjustments, stay disciplined against his routes, and finish tackles when he gets the ball in space. One missed assignment could allow Jeudy to swing momentum in Cleveland's favor.

Raheim Sanders could become more important if Judkins is unavailable or unable to handle his usual workload. He has recorded nine carries for 43 yards this season, and Cleveland may need him to shoulder additional responsibility if Judkins has physical limitations.

That possibility complicates the Ravens' preparation. Baltimore must maintain its gap discipline and tackle consistently regardless of which running back is on the field. If Sanders receives more opportunities, the Ravens cannot assume Cleveland's rushing attack will lose its effectiveness simply because its workload is distributed differently.

Isaiah McGuire has recorded 14 tackles, including four tackles for loss, and two sacks. Those numbers reflect his ability to disrupt plays behind the line of scrimmage, making him a defender the Ravens' offensive line must account for when establishing the running game and protecting the quarterback.

Baltimore needs to identify McGuire's alignment and recognize where he could attack the pocket. Letting him penetrate the backfield could put the offense behind the chains, creating longer passing situations where Cleveland's defense can play more aggressively. Limiting those negative plays will be important to keeping the Ravens' offense on schedule.

Adin Huntington has contributed 17 tackles and 1.5 sacks, giving Cleveland another option along its defensive front . His production adds to the challenge for an offensive line that must recognize multiple potential sources of pressure rather than concentrating exclusively on the Browns' best-known pass rushers.

The Ravens must communicate effectively and avoid allowing Huntington to win cleanly at the point of attack. Whether Cleveland uses him to pressure the quarterback or disrupt the ground game, Baltimore's ability to handle its assignments will help determine whether the offense can sustain drives.

Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has recorded 22 tackles, including 11 solo stops, and two pass breakups. He provides Cleveland with useful depth at safety and has shown he can contribute both in tackling situations and against the pass.

For Baltimore, the challenge is figuring out where McNeil-Warren fits in Cleveland's coverage structure. The Ravens need to identify the defensive look before the snap, avoid forcing throws into crowded areas, and take advantage of openings when the Browns commit defenders elsewhere. Even a depth safety can influence a game if an offense misreads the coverage or allows him to make a play.

Cleveland's supporting cast may not receive the same attention as its headline players, but each of these five contributors offers a different way to complicate Baltimore's afternoon. The Ravens must stay disciplined, execute their assignments, and resist the temptation to overlook anyone who could turn a routine play into a pivotal moment.
